title: Science Reveals Unauthorized Gene Therapy Trial Killed Chinese Girl
summary: Science magazine published an exclusive investigation on July 23, 2026, revealing that a 6-year-old girl died at Xinhua Hospital in Shanghai in March 2025 after receiving an experimental base-editing gene therapy for a rare monogenic disease, and the incident was never publicly reported. This case exposes severe lapses in China&\#x27;s clinical trial oversight, as researchers allegedly bypassed national regulatory approval using a hospital exemption, and failed to report the death. It could undermine public trust in gene editing therapies and prompt stricter global regulations for such experimental treatments. The girl received trillions of AAV viral vectors via spinal injection to target brain neurons, but died 7 days later from a severe immune reaction. Her parents paid over $800,000, and the ClinicalTrials.gov record had not been updated for over a year.
context: Base editing is a next-generation gene editing technology that can precisely change one DNA base to another without cutting the DNA double strand. AAV \(adeno-associated virus\) is commonly used as a vector to deliver therapeutic genes, but high doses can trigger immune responses. In China, certain clinical trials can be conducted under a &\#x27;hospital exemption&\#x27; without national review, a loophole that reportedly enabled this trial.
